answer.text: Recognition and regulation of stock exchanges, listing of securities, and regulation of contracts in securities
Only the registration of stock brokers

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook explains that the SCRA 1956 was enacted to prevent undesirable transactions in securities by regulating the business of dealing in securities. It places stock exchanges, contracts in securities, and listing of securities under the jurisdiction of the Central Government and prescribes how exchanges and securities transactions are governed. The Trap: SCRA is not limited to broker registration, and it does not cover taxation or company-law matters. Those topics sit under separate statutes that the workbook does not bring into this provision. Note: Anchor SCRA's scope to the workbook trio: regulating exchanges, listing of securities, and contracts in securities, with Central Government jurisdiction.
